Matilda Is an Aussie-Built Sprinter That Makes Long Off-Grid Trips Feel Like a Luxury Stay
19 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Summit Vans Australia
North America is packed with companies that create awesome adventure-ready camper vans. If you were to go someplace else to find a similar level of quality, my best bet would be Australia - Aussies really know how to transform vehicles into adventure-ready homes on wheels, as proven by the variety of builds you can find on the market. Today, I'm checking out a fresh conversion that nicely balances ruggedness and comfort.
Meet Matilda, a build based on a 2025 AWD Mercedes-Benz Sprinter with a 144" wheelbase and a high roof. It was created by Summit Vans, an Australia-based company specializing in camper vans built on the Sprinter platform.
This rig is definitely an eye-catcher, not only because it's finished in a beautiful Pebble Grey paint, but also because it sports a variety of exterior mods .
For instance, you can tell this rig was designed with off-roading in mind due to its wheel and tire combo - it rides on black Summit Vans wheels wrapped in Toyo Open Country all-terrain tires.
Before it made any modification or addition to the van, Summit Vans did a GVM (Gross Vehicle Mass) upgrade that offers an extra 727 lb. (330 kg) of payload capacity for a total of 9,766 lb. (4,430 kg). It comprises an upgraded rear leaf spring and an Outback bracket reinforcement. The van also sports Falcon adjustable shocks.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Summit Vans Australia Cars and vans already have a high chance of suffering paint chips and scratches when driving normally. When going off the beaten path, they're basically unavoidable. That's why many builders opt to coat certain elements in truck bed liner.
On this van, the bumpers, the grille, and side rocker panels are coated in Raptor liner. A nice aesthetic touch is that the badges are satin black. Furthermore, at the rear, Summit Vans installed a step and a spare tire carrier/ladder combo.
A van's roof offers valuable space that can be used for storage or for attaching accessories. On top of this rig, you'll come across a Weldbeat rack that holds a Fiamma awning, a front-facing Lightforce LED light bar, and two 200 W solar panels. The roof is also prepped for the installation of a Starlink Mini antenna.
Like many premium Sprinter-based camper vans, this rig sports a set of flares. Flares, also known as pods or capsules, are designed to increase the van width to allow you to fit a bed in an east to west arrangement.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Summit Vans Australia Flares are so popular on Sprinters because the model is slightly narrower than other camper van base vehicle options, like the Ford Transit or the Ram ProMaster. This van's Summit flares are coated in Raptor liner and come with half-slider windows. Other notable exterior mods are power and water connections and Weldbeat side steps.
Inside is the even more impressive bit. Slide the door open and a tastefully designed, space-maximizing interior will greet you. It has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space.
The open layout is super useful despite you losing some privacy and insulation, as it lets you use the cabin not just when driving. What makes this possible is the fact that the driver and passenger seats are mounted on swivel bases.
Regarding aesthetics, the customer opted for wall panels upholstered in grey woven outdoor fabric, dark grey laminated cabinetry, a slatted bamboo ceiling with recessed LED light strips, and warm wood-imitating vinyl plank flooring.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Summit Vans Australia Dead ahead of the entrance, Summit Vans added one of the two kitchen units. It offers a decent amount of counter space and integrates a 130-liter Dometic fridge with a tiny freezer compartment.
Above the counter, you get a microwave oven and the "command center" for the rig's utilities. The latter includes a thermostat, a touchscreen display that lets you monitor and control the power and water systems, dimmer light switches, and switches for a water pump, shower fan, and more.
The other kitchen unit is on the passenger side, by the entrance. It features a deep black stainless steel sink and a sizeable countertop. You can use a portable stove for cooking, and a Maxxair vent fan will draw out the smells and fumes from cooking.
Five drawers and a cabinet underneath the sink are available for storage. Moreover, the largest kitchen drawer can double as a step to climb into bed.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Summit Vans Australia On the opposite side, you'll find a surprisingly roomy bathroom behind a tall mirror door. It boasts a shower with a handheld wand, a wall-integrated vent, and an OGO Origin composting toilet. It also has an all-white aesthetic with white acrylic walls.
The bathroom doubles as a drying room for your gear, as it has a duct that pumps hot air into the space. What's more, there are L-Tracks that let you easily hang your items for drying - you can also use them to attach a clothesline.
You get a comfy bedroom all the way back inside the van. It has a cozy setup with two overhead cabinets with bamboo sliding steps, L-Tracks on the walls, and a ceiling A/C unit that can quickly cool off the interior when needed.
The space underneath the bedroom serves as a garage that's accessible from both inside and outside the van. Two tall boxes on the sides offer additional storage space and accommodate the utility systems.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Summit Vans Australia Loading and unloading items was made as easy as possible thanks to a pull-out tray with heavy-duty slides. Moreover, two rear door gas struts make it easier for you to pop the doors open and prevent them from slamming shut or hitting the sides of the van.
Power is on the left side – the electrical system's highlights are two 410 Ah batteries and a 3,000 W inverter. Three charging sources help keep the batteries topped off at all times: solar power , shore power, and DC-DC charging while the engine is running.
As for plumbing, the van is equipped with a freshwater tank, an under-mounted greywater tank, a water filtration system, and an outdoor shower connection. A Dieselheat DH9 hydronic system provides both hot water and heated air.
All in all, Matilda by Summit Vans blends a calm, natural interior with a roam-ready exterior setup. Long trips will be a breeze in this camper van thanks to the myriad of creature comforts and systems.
